usefulness.use_case: Grading programming labs at scale (CS1/CS2 courses)
usefulness.example: 300 students submit 'sort n integers'. The agent grades all of them overnight under identical limits. A student whose bubble sort times out on n = 100000 receives the failing input size, the measured O(n^2) growth curve and the hottest loop line, instead of a bare 'time limit exceeded'.
usefulness.benefit: Consistent, explainable grades in minutes; teaching assistants only look at flagged or borderline submissions.

usefulness.example: A company runs 500 candidate submissions for an 'add two integers safely' task. The agent ranks them by correctness, overflow handling and memory safety, and every rejection is backed by a concrete failing input such as '2147483647 1'.
usefulness.benefit: Fast first-round filtering where every decision can be justified metric by metric.

usefulness.example: Two submissions reach a similarity of 0.93 (threshold 0.85) even though every variable was renamed and every comment rewritten. The agent flags the pair with the matching line ranges, so the instructor inspects 2 files instead of 300. A third submission matches a solution generated by an LLM for the same statement and is flagged as a suspected LLM copy.
usefulness.benefit: Review time goes only to suspicious cases, and the evidence (lines, similarity) is already prepared.

usefulness.use_case: Self-check before the deadline / continuous integration for assignments
usefulness.example: A student's qsort solution passes the visible sample, but the agent's generated boundary case '2 / 0 -2147483648' shows that the comparator 'return a - b' overflows. The minimized counterexample and the suggested fix arrive before the student submits.
usefulness.benefit: Finds bugs that fixed test suites miss and teaches with the smallest input that breaks the program.

limitations.example: add_magic_value.c prints 0 whenever the first number is 4242. It passes 10/10 hidden tests and all 18 generated edge cases and is graded 97.9/100, because neither the tests nor the generators happen to produce 4242.
limitations.mitigation: Larger random budgets and instructor-specified 'must-test' values reduce the risk but never remove it; suspicious special-casing still needs a human reader.

limitations.limitation: Complexity is estimated from measured operation counts, not proven
limitations.example: sort_memmove_insertion.c finds each insertion point by binary search and shifts with memmove(). Its O(n^2) work happens inside libc, which gcov does not instrument, so the executed-line count grows like n log n, the agent reports 'O(n log n) confirmed' and grades it 99.8/100. Likewise a quicksort with a first-element pivot is O(n log n) on the random inputs used for measuring, but O(n^2) on sorted input.
limitations.mitigation: Include adversarial (sorted) inputs and a large hidden test that only an efficient solution passes within the time limit.

limitations.limitation: Similarity-based copy detection has false positives and false negatives
limitations.example: For 'add two integers', two honest solutions are almost the same token stream; the agent avoids flagging them only because of reference-code subtraction and the minimum-shared-fingerprints rule. Conversely, a student who takes an LLM answer and rewrites loops (for -> while), splits functions and reorders statements drops below 0.85 and is not flagged. When a pair is flagged, both students are flagged: the agent cannot tell who copied whom.
limitations.mitigation: Flags are review signals, never automatic verdicts; the instructor decides after reading the matched lines.

limitations.limitation: Verdicts depend on the platform and on external models
limitations.example: On Windows (MinGW) `long` is 32 bits, so a solution that sums into `long` overflows and fails tests that pass on Linux; ASan is unavailable there, so memory_safety falls back to UBSan trap mode and a leaking program loses no points. The LLM readability score can also change after `ollama pull` updates the model weights, and a program running at 0.95-1.05 s CPU can flip between AC and TLE across machines.
limitations.mitigation: Run official grading in the provided Linux/Docker image, keep the LLM response cache with the course records, and keep the hidden tests far from the time limit; every report records tool versions and hashes.
